In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the novel oxovanadium (IV) complexes exhibit highly cytotoxicity against three tumor cells, which is related to the DNA-binding ability, hydroxyl radical-scavenging ability, and cell cycle arrest of the compounds, especially the complex [VO(PAHn)(phen)].

all the four complexes exhibit good DNA-binding properties and antitumor activities against three different tumor cells, and complex 4 exhibits the strongest DNA-binding ability and complex 1 the highest antitumor activities.
the novel oxovanadium complexes are promising antitumor agents, which may be attributed to the intercalative binding mode of the complexes with DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have synthesized a series of oxovanadium(III) complexes with substituted hydrazide ligands.

four oxovanadium(4) complexes with different ligands, PAHN and PAH, have been prepared, and their interaction abilities with DNA have been investigated by UV–vis, fluorescence, and circular dichroism spectroscopy.

four novel oxovanadium (IV) complexes with isoniazid derivatives have been synthesized and characterized, their DNA binding and antitumor properties have been investigated, and their hydroxyl scavenging properties were also evaluated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the novel oxovanadium complexes have potential for use as antitumor agents.
a novel oxovanadium complex with substituted isoniaizid exhibits highly cytotoxic activity and can induce significant apoptosis in SK-NSH cells.

the oxovanadium( IV) complexes with substituted hydrazones of isoniazid are promising antitumor agents, and the most promising one is the oxovanadium complex of 4-pyidyl-2-((2-hydroxy-1-naphthalene)hydrazono)acetohydrazide.
